# OpenMantel

> OpenMantel is a free, open source (MIT) digital picture frame that you host yourself. It is a do-it-yourself project for people who self-host. A frame is a monitor with a small computer attached that runs a browser full screen, such as a Raspberry Pi, an Intel N100 mini PC, or a Mac mini. It does not work with store-bought digital photo frames. You manage photos and frames from your phone, and the photos stay on your own server.

OpenMantel runs as one Node.js process with SQLite, on a small VPS or a homelab server, installed with Docker Compose. Frames pair like a TV streaming stick: a frame shows a code and you approve it on your phone. A new install opens in demo mode with 15 sample photos, and switches to live with the owner's first upload. There are no sign-ups, no tracking, and no hosted service.

Key features: start a slideshow on every frame or one; random or sequential order that repeats forever; tags, presets, and hand-picked playlists built by drag and drop; whole photos with no cropping, on a matte or blurred backdrop, with captions; offline playback on frames; iPhone HEIC support, with location data removed from everything a frame receives; per-photo metadata; export of every original; and guarded bulk deletes.

## Docs

- [Demo](https://openmantel.com/demo/): what a frame shows, playing 25 sample photos in the browser
- [README](https://github.com/cschweda/openmantel#readme): features, screenshots, why it's self-hosted, installation, frame setup, and development
- [Self-hosting guide](https://github.com/cschweda/openmantel/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md): homelab and reverse proxy setups, updates, backups, troubleshooting
- [Design](https://github.com/cschweda/openmantel/blob/main/docs/00-master-design.md): architecture, data model, API, frame client
- [Security](https://github.com/cschweda/openmantel/blob/main/docs/06-security.md): threat model and controls
- [Security audits](https://github.com/cschweda/openmantel#security-audits): red/blue team audit findings and mitigations, newest first
